title.zh: 我们怎样理解两个人之间的关系
title.en: How Do We Understand the Relationship Between Two People?

summary.zh: 完整的中层方法：把人物倾向、互动机制与情境创作分层。
summary.en: A complete middle-layer method that separates character tendencies, interaction mechanisms, and situational storytelling.

body.zh: # 我们怎样理解两个人之间的关系 版本：v0.1｜2026-09-07｜观点与方法候选稿 **我们的出发点：人物倾向提供材料，双方怎样回应彼此构成关系，情境与选择推动关系变化。** 一个组名可以收纳许多故事；它最有价值的地方，是让人看到这两个人放在一起，会反复碰到什么问题。 这篇文章提出本项目自己的整理方法。它借鉴[心理学底层](01_心理学底层.md)中的一般关系研究，具体六种机制的编排、四轴比较、命名和剧情写法由本项目提出，尚未作为一套关系预测模型得到验证。 ## 1. 三层内容各自回答什么 | 层次 | 读者的问题 | 内容职责 | 内容身份 | |---|---|---|---| | 心理学底层 | 人与人的互动有哪些值得理解的机制？ | 讲清研究的问题、结论、方法与适用范围 | 既有研究的通俗整理 | | 我们的观点中层 | 用这些知识，怎样分析这16个人物？ | 明确取舍、观察步骤与创作方法 | 本项目提出的方法 | | 两型关系上层 | 这一对叫什么，有什么可聊、可写、可画？ | 给出组名、双向视角、场景与转折 | 基于角色的情境创作 | 读者可以从任意一层进入。从一个组名往下看，能找到它使用的关系机制；继续往下看，能知道相关研究真正支持什么。从研究往上看，也能理解我们在哪一步加入了自己的解释与创作。 ## 2. 四个问题，要分别问两个人 先把A与B各自的四轴展开。每一轴只说明相关情境中的相对优先，不把一个人固定成永远相同的反应。 | 四轴问题 | A与B各自要说明的事 | 放在一起时值得追问的事 | |---|---|---| | **争什么：利／权** | 更优先保住资源收益，还是决定权与地位确认？ | 两个人能否同时得到所需？是否抢同一份东西？谁有权分配？ | | **怎么推：谋／压** | 更常重排信息、关系和选项，还是直接提高拒绝成本？ | 两种路径能否接续？是否互相破坏？谁承担出面的成本？ | | **何时停：用／惩** | 外部目标达成后，让对方继续付代价是否仍有价值？ | 一人认为事已结束，另一人是否认为还欠一笔？ | | **如何呈现：饰／蔑** | 行动或事后解释更依赖规范与体面辩护，还是较少依赖这种认可？ | 谁需要对外解释？谁可能配合、利用或拆掉这层解释？ | 例如，掮客与操盘手同为谋、用、饰，区别集中在利与权。我们因此可以提出一个关系问题：如果收益与决定权能够分别满足，他们怎样交易；如果操盘手为了决定权改变了分配，掮客又会怎样回应？这给出了写作起点，后续还需要交代具体任务和双方筹码。 **定义核对。** 本稿以《核心模型与产品定义 v1.0》为准。“谋”可以公开设计局面，“压”可以通过精密程序施加压力。既有《理论基础与模型说明 v0.1》部分段落把谋写得更偏隐蔽，本稿不沿用这一收窄。人物资产的道具与动作可提供意象，其内部隐藏身份不作为现实职业或人格诊断输出。 ## 3. 六种关系机制 这些机制可以同时发生。每张关系卡挑出最能解释该场景的两到三种，方便读者继续阅读；标签数量不表示关系强度。 ### M01 共谋与争位：同一局里，各自想保住什么 **我们的观点。** 一对人物能不能并肩，先看共同结果怎样产生、结果由谁分配。相同目标可能让人同路，也可能让人争抢唯一位置；不同目标有时反而允许交换。我们把“目标能否一起满足”和“谁控制达成目标的条件”放在人物相似度之前。 值得观察四件事：共同任务是否真实存在；收益与决定权能否拆分；双方各自掌握什么；一方失去另一方后有多少替代选择。实际关系权力由这些条件形成，不能从“权型”这个字直接读出。 **自拟场景。** 掮客提供渠道，操盘手协调各方。约定的收益和决策范围都得到承认时，他们可以相互需要；当渠道变得可替代，原来的分配也可能受到挑战。关系的反转来自筹码变化，不需要任何人突然换型。 **写作支点：** “我们在一起能做成什么？”“做成以后，谁还有必要留下？” 研究路径：相互依赖理论与权力—依赖分析。[S01](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.psych.54.101601.145059)、[S02](https://doi.org/10.2307/2089716)。研究支持从情境和依赖关系分析互动；上述角色情节是本稿创作。 ### M02 镜像与互补：认得出你的招，也可能接得上你的招 **我们的观点。** 相似的行为语言容易制造“你懂我”的感觉，也容易使两人抢占同一位置。不同手段能成为分工，也能产生方法之争。我们同时保留“共同语言”“共同盲点”“可以分工的差异”“彼此踩到的差异”，不给相同或相反预设一个总评价。 要把三件事分开：双方事实上有多像；双方觉得彼此有多像；当前行为能否配合。人际互补研究讨论的支配与亲和，也不等于我们四轴中的权与饰。 **自拟场景。** 两位掮客都听得懂交易中的保留条件，谈判可以很省话；如果两人都希望对方先亮出真实份额，共同语言又会变成相互防备。操盘手与铁腕者则可能分别安排路径、推进执行，但也可能争论谁有资格改变计划。 **写作支点：** “你做得到我做不到的部分，还是你正在占我的位置？” 研究路径：目标与行为互补、互动节奏及实际／知觉相似。[S03](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.72.3.592)、[S04](https://doi.org/10.1037/a0016232)、[S05](https://doi.org/10.1177/0146167214557002)、[S06](https://doi.org/10.1177/0265407508096700)。这些研究也提示：互动配合、主观满意和长期关系质量要分别讨论。 ### M03 关系错账：同一件付出，被记进了不同账本 **我们的观点。** 很多冲突发生在双方对“这段关系应该怎么算”没有达成一致时。一个人把帮助理解为交换，另一个人当作自己人之间的照应；一个人在谈平分，另一个人在谈资历；一个人以为钱付清了，另一个人还在等被承认。 我们用四种通俗问题检查当前规则：是否按需要互助；是否按身份排序；是否要求一人一次、等量回报；是否按投入和回报比例计算。这些问法借鉴关系模式理论，但现实关系可以在不同议题上采用不同规则。不能把利型固定成只懂交换，也不能把权型固定成永远要求服从。 **自拟场景。** 掮客以为已经按约补足损失，笑面客认为那只还了利益账，没有回应被轻慢的一笔。同一份补偿，可能被一方当作结束，被另一方当作敷衍。 **写作支点：** “你以为你已经还了什么？对方以为你还欠什么？” 研究路径：交换关系与共同关系、关系模式理论。[S07](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.37.1.12)、[S08](https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-295X.99.4.689)。“错账”是我们的通俗整理名，没有另设心理量表。 ### M04 互激与停火：一轮回应，怎样把下一轮推得更远 **我们的观点。** 关系里的角色会随议题变化。先看这一次谁要求改变、谁更想维持现状，再写追问、加码、沉默、拖延或反击。谋者也可能追得很紧，压者也可能拒绝回应；不要把两条手段路径直接套成焦虑或回避依恋。 每个循环至少写明三步：触发了什么；A怎样解释并回应；B怎样理解这次回应。写转折时再补上一个可观察的停止动作，例如暂停追加条件、回应一项明确诉求、交还选择权。停火、承担后果和重建信任可以是不同阶段。 **自拟场景。** 一位清算者追问谁承担损失，另一位拖延核对。前者把拖延解释为不认账，追加要求；后者把加码解释为谈不拢，更不愿回应。若双方先把已确认和有争议的事项分开，故事可能出现停火口；仅仅不再说话，不能自动写成问题已解决。 **写作支点：** “如果有一人不按上一轮的方式回应，剧情从哪里改写？” 研究路径：需求—退缩、相关元分析、调适研究。[S09](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.59.1.73)、[S10](https://doi.org/10.1080/03637751.2013.813632)、[S11](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.60.1.53)。本稿的“停火条件”是叙事与观察问题，不保证任何现实关系必然修复。 ### M05 台前与后台：同一句话，说给谁听会改变它的作用 **我们的观点。** 两个人之间可能还站着一个看不见的第三方：同事、朋友、组织、围观者，或者双方自己认可的规则。饰／蔑提供对这些认可的不同依赖方式；观众、证据和行动后果又会改变两人的表达。 我们关心：谁需要一个说得过去的版本；谁替谁背书；谁会在公开场合拆台；两人私下的共识能否承担公开后的后果。共同口径可以服务协调，也可能成为遮蔽事实的工具，需要把实际行为一并写清。 **自拟场景。** 掮客准备了一套各方都能接受的分配说法，投机客直接说出谁拿得更多。这可以是拆台的笑点，也可以成为追问不对等分配的起点。若没有需要辩护的行为，不能仅凭一个人措辞直接就把其判成蔑。 **写作支点：** “他们私下知道什么？公开时又各自愿意承认多少？” 研究路径：印象管理与道德脱离。[S12](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.46.3.598)、[S13](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.71.2.364)。二者分别涉及呈现与自我约束，本方法没有把它们合并为饰／蔑的现成测量证据。 ### M06 例外与共塑：这一次，因为是你，我做了怎样的选择 **我们的观点。** 最能让人物关系留下记忆的，常是一个有具体代价的例外：愿意把真实选项说清，愿意让对方拒绝，愿意支持对方自己认可的目标。例外需要由场景中的行动建立，不能从两个类型代码自动算出。 双向视角尤其重要。A可能已经为B改变惯常反应，B却只把它理解为普通合作；也可能两人都在靠近，却误读了对方的方式。共同成长要说明成长目标是谁选择的，不能把“塑造成我喜欢的样子”写成对方的自我实现。 **自拟场景。** 操盘手原本习惯先安排好所有路径，面对特定的人却把选项和后果一起摆出来，接受对方选另一条路。这个动作可以成为亲密的起点，但故事还需要写对方是否愿意回应、后来是否保持这种选择空间。 **写作支点：** “这个人平常会怎么做？这一次改变在哪里？对方认出了这个改变吗？” 研究路径：关系特异性、独特吸引、理想自我的支持及共同新奇活动。[S14](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0065-2601(08)60144-6)、[S15](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9280.2007.01897.x)、[S16](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.77.2.293)、[S17](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.78.2.273)。共同体验可以扩展关系素材，不能代替信任、责任与对具体伤害的处理。 ## 4. 情境需要另外补充的六类信息 四轴不测这些信息。写虚构故事时由作者设定，分析真实互动时需要观察或询问；不知道就保留不知道。 | 情境问题 | 最少写清什么 | 为什么会改变关系 | |---|---|---| | 共同任务 | 双方正在一起完成或争取什么 | 同一对人在共同任务与争抢名额时可能站在不同边 | | 依赖与替代 | 谁掌握信息、资源、许可，谁还有其他选择 | 实际筹码可能与人物的支配偏好相反 | | 当前议题 | 谁希望现状改变，谁暂时从现状获益 | 追问与退缩的位置会换人 | | 观众与规则 | 谁能看见，哪种解释必须成立 | 私下交易与公开表态可能互相牵制 | | 历史与投入 | 过去欠过什么、兑现过什么、误会过什么 | 同一行为会因为历史被读成好意或重复伤害 | | 自主与修复 | 能否拒绝、暂停、离开；谁愿意承担后果 | 这些选择决定剧情怎样发展，类型本身不给答案 | ## 5. 16种相同／不同结构，只用来找问题 按“目标、手段、终止、规范”顺序记录双方同或异，会得到16种结构。这里的“同”只表示同侧，不表示倾向强度、能力、立场或人生经历相同；“异”也不表示每次行为都会相反。 | 结构 | 优先追问的关系问题 | |---|---| | 同同同同 | 同样的做法，谁先拿到位置；双方能否识别自己的共同盲点？ | | 异同同同 | 方法相近，但最终拿收益还是拿决定权，能否分别满足？ | | 同异同同 | 要的相近，推进路径不同，能否接上对方的行动？ | | 同同异同 | 事情做到哪一步算结束，是否有一方仍认为代价不够？ | | 同同同异 | 实际目标与行动相近，对外解释的需要是否一致？ | | 异异同同 | 想要的和出招方式都不同，怎样找到共同任务？ | | 异同异同 | 可以使用相近的办法，但最后争什么、何时收手是否分歧？ | | 异同同异 | 目标和公开说法不同，会不会在同一次布局中互相拆台？ | | 同异异同 | 想去同一处，但推进速度、路径和停止条件如何协商？ | | 同异同异 | 手段与体面需求不同，谁承担出面及解释的成本？ | | 同同异异 | 前半程容易并行，收尾与公开解释是否开始分裂？ | | 异异异同 | 共同认可的一套说法，是否仍掩不住实际目标与行动分歧？ | | 异异同异 | 除了何时收手相近，双方还需要怎样的具体约定？ | | 异同异异 | 熟悉对方的方法，会成为谈判语言还是相互预判？ | | 同异异异 | 唯一相近的目标，足不足以维持接下来的协作？ | | 异异异异 | 四处差异都存在时，什么外部任务或个人选择能让两人入局？ | 例如，T01×T09只有目标轴不同，记作“异同同同”；T13×T16在目标、手段上相同，在终止、规范上不同，记作“同同异异”。 相同轴的数量可以用于完整性检查，不能相加得到适配、危险或好磕分数。关系卡中的具体例子也不因只差一轴就必然比差四轴的组合更顺利。 ## 6. 一张关系卡怎样写出来 1. **展开人物。** 读双方四轴与角色语义，区分已给定的倾向和另外设定的能力、经历。 2. **比较四个问题。** 记录共同点与分歧，选出最值得写的两处；其余轴也要核对，防止文案与定义相反。 3. **放入情境。** 明确一个任务、一份稀缺资源或一个尚未解决的问题，给双方不同的位置。 4. **分别写视角。** A可能怎样理解B，B可能怎样理解A。用“可能”表明这是解释候选，避免读心式断言。 5. **挑选机制。** 选择两到三个机制；在结构依据、三条支线、转折或停火字段中，要能看见它们具体在哪一步起作用。 6. **展开三条支线。** 写合作如何成立、冲突如何出现、亲密例外如何由自愿行动建立；每条都要有自己的成立条件。 7. **寻找转折。** 改变一项情境条件，观察双方怎样重新回应；再写一个具体停火动作，避免只用“沟通一下”收尾。 8. **凝结为名字。** 从双方反复交锋的物件、动作、空间或矛盾中选一个意象，让开场短句承担“一句话解释为什么是这一对”。 这套顺序是可重复的编辑检查。作者仍需为任务、筹码和选择提供具体设定，再把它们写成可以观察的互动。 ## 7. 关系如何随时间改写 我们用四个时间点整理故事：**入局、绑定、裂缝、改写**。四个词用于定位剧情节点；同一故事可以跳过、倒置或重复其中任何一段。 - **入局：** 为什么接近？一次机会、共同任务、相似感，还是某个只有对方能回应的需要？ - **绑定：** 为什么继续？双方获得了什么，又分别付出了什么？ - **裂缝：** 哪一次回应被重新解释？收益变了、权限变了、观众出现了，还是原来的规则被单方面改写？ - **改写：** 哪个行动使关系走向合作、冲突、亲密、保持距离或结束？双方是否都接受新的安排？ 以“筹码组”为例：因资源整合而入局，因收益和决定权的交换而绑定，因单方面改分配而出现裂缝；重新说明条件、承认拒绝权，可以开启另一条支线。每个箭头都要有行为或条件作为桥梁。 ## 8. 命名如何兼顾识别与二创 16型不同类型两两组合有120组，加入16组同型组合，共136组。每组保留一个主名，A×B与B×A共享主名；双方视角仍分别保存。名字覆盖的是人物组合，合作、宿敌、CP是该组合之下的可选叙事分支。同卡中的分支可以是不同时间线，读者可选择其中一条展开，不必把所有片段拼成唯一故事。 命名主要使用四种方式：共同物件，如筹码与余账；接续动作，如收网；共同空间，如相邻的座位与同一舞台；核心矛盾，如共同口径被一句话穿破。名字读起来应顺口，能联想到关系，又能容纳多种情境。 本版所有组合名均为项目拟定的候选名。它们没有被写成心理学分类，也没有被伪装成已经流行的社区叫法。以后收录用户别称时，另存名称、来源、作者署名偏好和收录时间；是否采用为主名，是一次明确的内容版本更新。 当前名字的首要验收是：能认出这一对；一句话能解释；与其他组区分；换一个剧情仍能成立。名字不能保证社区一定使用，少数熟人短聊只用于发现难读、误解或违和之处。 ## 9. 网站读者可以直接看到的说明 > 每一对人物，都有一个可以继续写下去的名字。我们从他们争什么、怎样推动局面、何时收手和如何面对规则出发，整理共同点、分歧与转折。搭档、宿敌和CP是故事可能走向的不同方向；具体关系由情境和双方选择展开。想继续了解，可以沿着关系卡中的机制，阅读我们的分析方法与相关心理学研究。 关系卡旁保留一句短说明即可：“人物关系创作参考；不预测现实中的配对结果。”更详细的研究范围放在方法与来源页，避免每个段落重复同一长段声明。 ## 10. 编辑时如何判断内容是否足够好 **结构正确。** 136组完整、对称查找不重复、16组同型有清楚的情境位置、轴含义与名称映射一致。 **解释具体。** 读完能说出这对人物共同做什么、最可能在哪个情节起分歧、至少一个怎样改变情境的办法。若去掉姓名后可以无差别放进几十组，说明仍需改写。 **视角成对。** A的善意不能代替B的理解，A想要控制也不能当作B已经服从。单向误读本身可以构成剧情，但要写清它属于哪一方。 **转折可见。** 用交还选项、说明条件、停止追加要求等行动说明转变；不把“突然懂了”“命中注定”当成解释。 **来源诚实。** 研究支持一般机制，方法与组合内容注明由本项目提出。所有研究结论保留原来的证据性质，名称不承担诊断、坏度或关系健康排名。 **亲密有选择。** CP可以有矛盾和暗面，但将尊重拒绝、承担后果和自愿支持作为可写的关系变化；戏剧张力本身不证明现实中的伤害值得忍受。 本轮由Agent完成资料、内容和数据检查。后续如使用真人反馈，按项目既定资源，最多与三四位熟人短聊，重点问是否读懂和是否想继续看；不将其表述为统计验证或心理测量验证。
body.en: # How Do We Understand the Relationship Between Two People? Version: v0.1 | 2026-09-07 | Candidate perspective and method draft **Our starting point: character tendencies supply the raw material; the ways two people respond to each other constitute their relationship; situations and choices drive that relationship to change.** One pairing name can hold many stories. Its greatest value is showing what problems these two people may encounter again and again when placed together. This article presents this project's own framework. It draws on general relationship research in [Psychological Foundations](01_%E5%BF%83%E7%90%86%E5%AD%A6%E5%BA%95%E5%B1%82.md). The arrangement of the six specific mechanisms, the four-axis comparison, the naming system, and the approach to writing storylines were developed by this project and have not been validated as a relationship-prediction model. ## 1. What Each of the Three Layers Answers | Layer | The reader's question | Responsibility | Status | |---|---|---|---| | Psychological foundations | What mechanisms in human interaction are worth understanding? | Explain the research questions, findings, methods, and scope | An accessible synthesis of existing research | | Our middle-layer perspective | How can we use this knowledge to analyze these 16 characters? | Define our choices, observation steps, and creative method | A method proposed by this project | | Pair-relationship layer | What is this pair called, and what can we discuss, write, or draw about them? | Provide a pairing name, two-way perspectives, scenes, and turning points | Character-based situational storytelling | Readers can enter at any layer. Starting from a pairing name and moving downward reveals the relationship mechanisms it uses; going farther shows what the relevant research actually supports. Starting from the research and moving upward also shows where our own interpretation and creative work enter the process. ## 2. Four Questions, Asked of Each Person Separately First expand A's and B's four axes. Each axis describes only a relative priority in relevant situations; it does not lock a person into the same response forever. | Four-axis question | What to establish for A and B separately | What to ask when they are together | |---|---|---| | **What do they contend for: Gain / Control** | Do they prioritize securing material returns, or decision-making authority and confirmation of status? | Can both get what they need? Are they competing for the same thing? Who has the right to allocate it? | | **How do they push: Strategy / Pressure** | Are they more likely to rearrange information, relationships, and options, or directly raise the cost of refusal? | Can the two approaches work in sequence? Do they undermine each other? Who bears the cost of acting openly? | | **When do they stop: Instrumental / Punitive** | Once the external goal has been achieved, is there still value in making the other person pay? | Does one person think the matter is over while the other believes a debt remains? | | **How do they present it: Justification / Disregard** | Do their actions or later explanations rely more on respectable, norm-based justification, or less on that kind of approval? | Who needs an explanation for outsiders? Who might support, exploit, or puncture that explanation? | For example, Broker and Puppet Master are both Strategy, Instrumental, and Justification; their difference lies in Gain versus Control. This lets us pose a relationship question: if returns and decision-making authority can be satisfied separately, how do they trade? If Puppet Master changes the allocation to secure authority, how does Broker respond? That is a starting point for writing; the specific task and each side's leverage still need to be established. **Definition check.** This draft follows *Core Model and Product Definitions v1.0*. Strategy may involve designing a situation openly, and Pressure may be applied through precise procedures. Some passages in the existing *Theoretical Foundations and Model Notes v0.1* frame Strategy as more covert; this draft does not adopt that narrower definition. Props and actions in the character assets may supply imagery, but concealed identities within those assets are not presented as real-world occupations or personality diagnoses. ## 3. Six Relationship Mechanisms These mechanisms may occur simultaneously. Each relationship card selects the two or three that best explain its scene, helping readers explore further; the number of tags does not indicate relationship intensity. ### M01 Collusion and the Contest for Position: What Does Each Person Want to Preserve in the Same Game? **Our perspective.** To understand whether two characters can work side by side, first examine how their shared outcome is produced and who allocates it. The same goal may put people on the same path or make them compete for a single position; different goals may sometimes enable exchange. We place “whether both goals can be satisfied” and “who controls the conditions for achieving them” ahead of character similarity. Four things deserve attention: whether a shared task truly exists; whether gains and decision-making authority can be separated; what each side controls; and how many alternatives either side has without the other. Actual power in a relationship arises from these conditions and cannot be read directly from the label “Control type.” **Original scenario.** Broker provides access while Puppet Master coordinates the parties. They may need each other while the agreed gains and scope of authority are both respected. If that access becomes replaceable, the original allocation may be challenged. The reversal comes from a change in leverage; no one needs to switch type abruptly. **Writing prompts:** “What can we accomplish together?” “Once it is done, who still needs to remain?” Research pathways: interdependence theory and power-dependence analysis. [S01](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.psych.54.101601.145059), [S02](https://doi.org/10.2307/2089716). The research supports analyzing interaction through situations and dependencies; the character storyline above is original to this draft. ### M02 Mirroring and Complementarity: Recognizing Your Move—and Perhaps Following It **Our perspective.** Similar behavioral languages readily create a sense of “you understand me,” but they can also lead two people to compete for the same position. Different methods may support a division of labor or produce a dispute over approach. We retain all four possibilities—shared language, shared blind spots, differences that enable coordination, and differences that cause friction—without assigning an overall positive or negative verdict to similarity or opposition. Keep three things separate: how similar the two actually are; how similar they perceive each other to be; and whether their current behavior can work together. Dominance and affiliation in interpersonal complementarity research are also not equivalent to Control and Justification in our four axes. **Original scenario.** Two Brokers both understand the unstated reservations in a deal, so negotiations can be economical. If each wants the other to reveal their true share first, that shared language turns into mutual wariness. Puppet Master and Enforcer may divide the work between arranging the route and driving execution, yet still dispute who is entitled to change the plan. **Writing prompt:** “Can you do the part I cannot, or are you taking my place?” Research pathways: goal and behavioral complementarity, interaction rhythms, and actual versus perceived similarity. [S03](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.72.3.592), [S04](https://doi.org/10.1037/a0016232), [S05](https://doi.org/10.1177/0146167214557002), [S06](https://doi.org/10.1177/0265407508096700). These studies also suggest that coordination in interaction, subjective satisfaction, and long-term relationship quality should be discussed separately. ### M03 Mismatched Ledgers: The Same Contribution Is Entered in Different Books **Our perspective.** Many conflicts arise because the parties have not agreed on how the relationship should be accounted for. One treats help as an exchange, while the other sees it as care among one's own people; one talks about equal shares, while the other talks about seniority; one thinks payment settled the matter, while the other is still waiting for acknowledgment. We examine the current rules through four plain questions: Is help given according to need? Is priority ranked by status? Is turn-taking or equal repayment expected? Are contributions and returns calculated proportionally? These questions draw on relational models theory, but real relationships may use different rules for different matters. Gain types cannot be reduced to exchange alone, and Control types cannot be treated as always demanding obedience. **Original scenario.** Broker believes the agreed compensation has made good the loss. Smiler believes it repaid only the material account and did not address the slight. The same compensation may count as closure to one person and a brush-off to the other. **Writing prompt:** “What do you think you have already repaid? What does the other person think you still owe?” Research pathways: exchange and communal relationships; relational models theory. [S07](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.37.1.12), [S08](https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-295X.99.4.689). “Mismatched ledgers” is our accessible organizing term, not a separate psychological scale. ### M04 Escalation and Ceasefire: How One Response Pushes the Next Round Further **Our perspective.** Roles within a relationship change with the issue. First identify who is asking for change this time and who wants to preserve the status quo; then write the questioning, escalation, silence, delay, or counterattack. A Strategist may pursue intensely, and a Pressure type may refuse to respond. Do not map these two modes directly onto anxious or avoidant attachment. Each cycle should specify at least three steps: what triggered it; how A interpreted and answered; and how B understood that answer. When writing a turn, add an observable stopping action, such as pausing further conditions, responding to one clear request, or returning the power to choose. A ceasefire, accepting consequences, and rebuilding trust may be separate stages. **Original scenario.** A Arbiter presses for an answer about who will bear the loss, while the other person delays verification. The former reads delay as refusal to acknowledge the debt and adds demands; the latter reads escalation as proof that agreement is impossible and withdraws further. If they first separate confirmed items from disputed ones, the story may find an opening for a ceasefire. Simply falling silent cannot automatically be written as resolution. **Writing prompt:** “If one person stops responding in the same way as the previous round, where does the story change?” Research pathways: demand-withdraw patterns, related meta-analysis, and accommodation research. [S09](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.59.1.73), [S10](https://doi.org/10.1080/03637751.2013.813632), [S11](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.60.1.53). This draft's “ceasefire conditions” are narrative and observational questions; they do not guarantee that any real relationship will be repaired. ### M05 Frontstage and Backstage: The Audience Changes What the Same Words Do **Our perspective.** An unseen third party may stand between two people: colleagues, friends, an organization, onlookers, or rules both recognize. Justification / Disregard describes different degrees of reliance on such approval; audiences, evidence, and the consequences of action also change how the two express themselves. We ask: Who needs a defensible account? Who vouches for whom? Who will contradict the other in public? Can their private understanding withstand the consequences of becoming public? A shared line can coordinate action, but it may also conceal facts, so the actual conduct must be made clear as well. **Original scenario.** Broker prepares an account of the allocation that every party can accept; Opportunist says outright who received more. This may be a comic act of puncturing the story, or the start of questioning an unequal allocation. If there is no conduct requiring justification, a person's wording alone is not enough to classify them as Disregard. **Writing prompt:** “What do they know in private, and how much will each admit in public?” Research pathways: impression management and moral disengagement. [S12](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.46.3.598), [S13](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.71.2.364). These concern presentation and self-restraint respectively; our method does not combine them into ready-made measurement evidence for Justification / Disregard. ### M06 Exceptions and Mutual Shaping: This Time, Because It Is You, What Choice Did I Make? **Our perspective.** What makes a character relationship memorable is often an exception with a concrete cost: choosing to state the real options clearly, allowing the other person to refuse, or supporting a goal the other person has chosen for themselves. An exception must be established through action in a scene; it cannot be calculated automatically from two type codes. The two-way perspective matters especially here. A may already have changed a habitual response for B, while B reads it as ordinary cooperation. Both may be moving closer yet misreading how the other does so. Shared growth must identify who chose the goal of growth; “shaping you into what I prefer” cannot be written as the other person's self-actualization. **Original scenario.** Puppet Master usually arranges every route in advance, but with one particular person presents the options and consequences together and accepts that person's choice of another route. This may begin an intimate bond, but the story must still show whether the other person chooses to respond and whether that room for choice remains later. **Writing prompt:** “What would this person normally do? What changed this time? Did the other person recognize the change?” Research pathways: relationship specificity, unique attraction, support for the ideal self, and shared novel activities. [S14](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0065-2601(08)60144-6), [S15](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9280.2007.01897.x), [S16](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.77.2.293), [S17](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.78.2.273). Shared experiences can broaden the material of a relationship; they cannot replace trust, responsibility, or addressing specific harm. ## 4. Six Additional Kinds of Situational Information The four axes do not measure this information. Authors set it when writing fiction; analysis of real interaction requires observation or questions. If it is unknown, leave it unknown. | Situational question | Minimum detail to establish | Why it changes the relationship | |---|---|---| | Shared task | What are the two trying to accomplish or obtain together? | The same pair may stand on different sides in a joint task and in a contest for one place. | | Dependence and alternatives | Who controls information, resources, or permission, and who has other options? | Actual leverage may run counter to a character's preference for dominance. | | Current issue | Who wants the status quo to change, and who currently benefits from it? | The pursuer and withdrawer can switch places. | | Audience and rules | Who can see, and what account must hold up? | Private deals and public positions may constrain each other. | | History and investment | What was owed, honored, or misunderstood in the past? | History can make the same behavior read as goodwill or repeated harm. | | Autonomy and repair | Can either person refuse, pause, or leave; who will accept the consequences? | These choices determine how the story develops; type alone supplies no answer. | ## 5. Sixteen Same/Different Structures, Used Only to Find Questions Recording whether the two match or differ in the order “goal, method, stopping point, norm” produces 16 structures. “Same” means only the same side of an axis, not the same strength, ability, position, or life experience. “Different” does not mean their behavior will oppose each other every time. | Structure | Priority relationship question | |---|---| | Same–Same–Same–Same | With the same approach, who secures the position first, and can they recognize their shared blind spots? | | Different–Same–Same–Same | Their methods are similar, but can material gain and decision-making authority be satisfied separately? | | Same–Different–Same–Same | They want similar things but use different routes; can their actions connect? | | Same–Same–Different–Same | At what point is the matter over, and does one side still think the price was insufficient? | | Same–Same–Same–Different | Their actual goals and actions are similar, but do they have the same need for an outward explanation? | | Different–Different–Same–Same | Their aims and methods differ; how can they find a shared task? | | Different–Same–Different–Same | They can use similar methods, but do they disagree about the final prize and when to stop? | | Different–Same–Same–Different | With different goals and public accounts, will they undermine each other within the same plan? | | Same–Different–Different–Same | They want to reach the same place; how will they negotiate pace, route, and stopping conditions? | | Same–Different–Same–Different | Their methods and need for respectability differ; who bears the cost of acting openly and explaining it? | | Same–Same–Different–Different | They may proceed together at first; do they split over how to finish and explain it publicly? | | Different–Different–Different–Same | Can a shared acceptable account still conceal their differences in goals and action? | | Different–Different–Same–Different | Apart from a similar stopping point, what specific agreements do they need? | | Different–Same–Different–Different | Does familiarity with the other's methods become a language for negotiation or a basis for anticipating each other? | | Same–Different–Different–Different | Is their one similar goal enough to sustain the cooperation that follows? | | Different–Different–Different–Different | With differences on all four axes, what external task or personal choice can bring them into the same game? | For example, T01 × T09 differ only on the goal axis, so they are Different–Same–Same–Same. T13 × T16 match on goal and method but differ on stopping point and norm, so they are Same–Same–Different–Different. The number of matching axes may be used as a completeness check. It cannot be added up into a compatibility, danger, or “good ship” score. Nor must a pair differing on only one axis have an easier relationship than one differing on all four. ## 6. How to Write a Relationship Card 1. **Expand the characters.** Read both characters' four axes and role semantics; distinguish given tendencies from separately established abilities and experiences. 2. **Compare the four questions.** Record commonalities and differences and select the two most worth writing about. Check the remaining axes as well so the copy does not contradict the definitions. 3. **Place them in a situation.** Establish a task, a scarce resource, or an unresolved problem, and give the two different positions within it. 4. **Write each perspective.** How might A understand B, and B understand A? Use “may” to mark these as candidate interpretations and avoid claims of mind-reading. 5. **Select mechanisms.** Choose two or three. Their concrete operation should be visible in the structural rationale, three story branches, turning point, or ceasefire fields. 6. **Develop three branches.** Show how cooperation becomes possible, how conflict emerges, and how an intimate exception is created through voluntary action. Each branch needs its own conditions. 7. **Find a turning point.** Change one situational condition and observe how both respond anew. Then write one concrete ceasefire action instead of ending with “they communicate.” 8. **Condense it into a name.** Choose an image from an object, action, space, or contradiction recurring between them. Let the opening line explain in one sentence why it belongs to this pair. This sequence is a repeatable editorial check. The author must still give the task, leverage, and choices concrete form, then write them as observable interaction. ## 7. How Relationships Are Rewritten Over Time We organize stories around four moments: **entry, binding, fracture, rewriting**. These terms locate story beats; a story may skip, reverse, or repeat any of them. - **Entry:** Why do they approach each other—an opportunity, a shared task, a sense of similarity, or a need only the other can answer? - **Binding:** Why do they stay? What does each gain, and what does each pay? - **Fracture:** Which response is reinterpreted? Did the gains change, authority shift, an audience appear, or the original rules change unilaterally? - **Rewriting:** What action moves the relationship toward cooperation, conflict, intimacy, distance, or an ending? Do both accept the new arrangement? Take the “Leverage Pair” as an example: they enter through resource integration, bind through an exchange of gains and decision-making authority, and fracture when one side changes the allocation. Restating the terms and acknowledging the right to refuse may open another branch. Every arrow needs an action or condition as its bridge. ## 8. Naming for Recognition and Fan Creation Pairing 16 distinct types produces 120 combinations; adding 16 same-type combinations yields 136. Each pair keeps one primary name, shared by A × B and B × A, while the two perspectives remain separate. The name covers the character combination. Partnership, rivalry, and close bonds are optional narrative branches beneath it. Branches on one card may represent different timelines; readers may develop one without combining every fragment into a single canonical story. Names mainly use four approaches: a shared object, such as leverage or an outstanding balance; a continuing action, such as drawing the net closed; a shared space, such as adjacent seats or the same stage; or a central contradiction, such as a shared line punctured by one sentence. A name should sound natural, evoke the relationship, and accommodate multiple situations. All pairing names in this version are project-created candidates. They are not presented as psychological classifications or disguised as community names already in popular use. If user-created aliases are collected later, record the name, source, author's attribution preference, and date collected separately. Adopting one as the primary name is an explicit content-version update. The current primary checks for a name are: readers can identify the pair; one sentence can explain it; it differs from other names; and it still works when the storyline changes. A name cannot guarantee community uptake. Short chats with a few acquaintances serve only to find wording that is hard to read, misleading, or jarring. ## 9. A Note Website Readers Can See Directly > Every pair of characters has a name whose story can continue. Starting from what they contend for, how they move a situation, when they stop, and how they face rules, we organize their common ground, differences, and turning points. Partners, rivals, and close bonds are different directions their story may take; the specific relationship unfolds through the situation and both people's choices. To learn more, follow the mechanisms on a relationship card to read our analytical method and the related psychological research. A short note beside each relationship card is enough: “A reference for creating character relationships; it does not predict real-world pairing outcomes.” Put the fuller discussion of research scope on the method and sources page so every passage need not repeat the same long disclaimer. ## 10. How Editors Judge Whether the Content Is Good Enough **Structurally correct.** All 136 pairs are present, reciprocal lookup creates no duplicates, the 16 same-type pairs have clear situational positions, and axis meanings agree with the name mapping. **Concretely explained.** After reading, someone can say what the pair does together, where a disagreement is most likely to emerge in the story, and at least one way a situational change could alter it. If removing the names leaves text that could be assigned indiscriminately to dozens of pairs, it still needs revision. **Perspectives come in pairs.** A's goodwill cannot substitute for B's understanding, and A's desire for control cannot be treated as B's submission. A one-sided misreading can itself create a story, but the writing must identify whose misreading it is. **The turn is visible.** Show change through actions such as returning options, stating conditions, or stopping additional demands. Do not use “they suddenly understood” or “it was destined” as explanations. **Sources are represented honestly.** Research supports general mechanisms; the method and pairing content are identified as this project's proposals. Every research claim retains its original evidentiary status, and names do not serve as diagnoses or rankings of badness or relationship health. **Intimacy involves choice.** A story of intimacy may contain conflict and darkness, but respect for refusal, acceptance of consequences, and voluntary support are available forms of relationship change. Dramatic tension alone does not show that real-world harm is worth enduring. This round of source, content, and data checks is performed by Agent. If human feedback is used later, follow the project's established resource constraint: brief chats with no more than three or four acquaintances, focused on whether they understand the material and want to keep reading. Do not present this as statistical validation or psychometric validation.
